sources: The monitoring deck's 330 clippings plus every page of all 15 full editions, including Dainik Savera's district pages (the deck's HT and Express slides were blank, so those papers come from their full editions). Relevant = about AAP, the Punjab government or a state matter.
takeaway: {negative_share} of the {relevant} relevant stories were negative and {positive_share} positive, a tougher day than 27 October. The Assembly's last day split the coverage: the water-rights and Kartarpur resolutions led front pages, but the House scuffle, the High Court fine over DA arrears and the Mansa body seizure drove the negatives, and BJP statements alone numbered 42. District pages were kinder: police action, paddy payments and 'Mera Ghar Mera Naam' property cards.
well: Water rights and Kartarpur owned the front pages.
The river-water resolutions (Rs 1.44 lakh crore sought from Rajasthan) and the Kartarpur corridor resolution made 13 front pages between them.
Hockey gave the CM a feel-good platform.
The Asian Champions Trophy opening in Jalandhar ran in 10 papers with 4 front pages, alongside the pitch to host the 2030 World Cup.
Police action is still the largest positive theme.
Army jawan among 7 held with 14 pistols and 20 kg heroin ran in 11 papers; district pages carried dozens of seizures, demolitions of smugglers' property and drug-hotspot meetings.
improve: Opposition statements hit a new high.
82 attacks (BJP 42, Congress 20, SAD 15, others 5) against 16 AAP replies. Jakhar's NIA letter, Bittu's liquor bottle and Dhillon's 'jungle raj' each ran in 5 or more papers.
Law and order is the story the opposition is winning.
The Mansa body seizure, the AAP sarpanch's son shot in Amritsar and the attack on police in Gurdaspur put crime on 7 front pages.
Courts and own ranks are adding pressure.
The HC fine on the Chief Secretary over DA and PSPCL dues ran in 12 papers. AAP MLAs Manuke and Gill criticised ministers in the House, and 46 leaders joined the BJP in Gurdaspur.
